@891
Channel Type
SPRINKLR_LIVE_CHAT

### Fetching Order Data

- 1

            Locate the "App Order ID" Field

              Below the Customer Details card, there is an **App Order ID** input field. The order number associated with this case is **KW3619614384056415** (also visible in the CRM panel as Order Number *8004795351*).
- 2

            Enter the Order ID or Leave Blank

              Enter a specific **App Order ID** to retrieve that single order's details. Leave the field blank and click **Get Order Data** to retrieve *all orders* linked to this customer account.
- 3

            Click "Get Order Data"

              The system fetches order status, delivery details, and product information from the backend. Use this data to confirm delivery status, identify wrong items, or check refund eligibility before responding.

## Historical Cases & Profile Properties

The right panel also surfaces the customer's interaction history and profile metadata, enabling agents to provide context-aware support.

(image)
🔍 Click to zoom
Image 4 — Profile Properties & Historical Cases
- ①

            Profile Properties

              Found in the centre panel when a profile is open. Shows the Sprinklr internal ID, name, phone, email, and **Channel Type**. The unique Sprinklr profile ID for Houda is *A_6990388ea094910703e79aef*, which is useful for internal lookups.
- ②

            Historical Cases

              Displays all previous cases linked to the customer. In this example, Case #51154 from **Feb 14, 2026** is shown with status Internal Hold. Use this to identify repeat issues, prior escalations, or whether a refund was already processed.
- ③

            Send SMS / Send Email

              From the profile header, agents can initiate outbound contact via **Send SMS** or **Send Email** directly from Sprinklr — useful for follow-ups on cases placed on Internal Hold.
- ④

            Apply Profile Macro

              The **Apply Profile Macro** button applies automation rules at the *contact/profile* level rather than the case level. This can tag a customer, update their profile status, or trigger a CRM workflow.

## Understanding & Applying Case Macros

Macros are pre-configured automation workflows that update multiple case fields in a single click. They standardise case management across the team and ensure consistent routing, SLA tagging, and status changes. Agents access macros via the **Apply Case Macro** button in the top navigation bar.

(image)
🔍 Click to zoom
Image 6 — Macro Selector Panel
📌 Remember:
Always verify the correct macro was choosen before clicking
Apply
. If you applied the wrong macro, Change it immediately.

### Available Macros

- ★

            Assign To Me

              Assigns the case directly to the logged-in agent. Use this when picking up an unassigned case from the queue. This also updates the **Assignee** field and may trigger SLA timers.
- ★

            Assign To X

              Assigns the case to a specific agent or team. A secondary field will appear to select the target agent. Used for warm handoffs between departments or shift changes.
- ★

            Awaiting Response

              Changes the case status to Awaiting Response. Apply this when you have replied to the customer and are waiting for their feedback. The SLA clock may pause in this state depending on your configuration.
- ★

            Internal Hold

              Applies the Internal Hold status and routes the case to the relevant internal team (e.g. *Content* department) for further investigation. As seen in this case, Tasnim Mohamed applied this macro to escalate to the Content team with an *External Email Escalation* action. This is used when the case cannot be resolved immediately and requires internal action.
- ★

            Resolved

              Closes the case as resolved. **This macro requires you to fill in Custom Properties** (see next section) before it can be applied. Resolving without completing mandatory fields will be blocked by the system.

📂 All Macros (10):
Beyond the 5 favourites, there are additional macros in the
All Macros
section. These cover edge cases like VIP escalations, technical queues, and partner-specific workflows. Always check with your team leader if unsure which macro applies.

## Completing the "Resolved" Macro — Custom Properties

When applying the **Resolved** macro, the system displays an *Apply Resolved* dialog requiring mandatory fields to be completed. This ensures every closed case has proper tagging for quality assurance and reporting.

(image)
🔍 Click to zoom
Image 8 — Apply Resolved · Custom Properties Form

### Field-by-Field Guide

- 1

            Order Number Optional

              Pre-filled if an order number was entered earlier (e.g. **8004795351**). If the case is not order-related (e.g. general enquiries), leave this blank. For exchange or delivery complaints, always enter the relevant order number.
- 2

            Contact Reason Required ●

              Select the most accurate reason from the dropdown that describes *why* the customer contacted support. Examples include: *Complaint – Wrong item (Exchange)*, *Delivery Delay*, *Refund Request*, *Product Enquiry*. Choosing the wrong reason skews reporting data — take care to select accurately.
- 3

            Concerned Department Required ●

              Select the department that handled or needs to action this case. In this example, **Content** was selected because the escalation involved a product listing/content issue. Other options typically include *Logistics*, *Operations*, *Finance*, and *Customer Service*.
- 4

            Action Status Required ●

              Describes how the case is being resolved from a *team action* perspective. Options include actions like **External Email Escalation** (already set in this case), *Refund Processed*, *Replacement Sent*, *Information Provided*, and similar. This field answers: *"What did we actually DO to resolve this?"*
- 5

            Click "Apply" to Resolve the Case

              Once all required fields (marked with a red dot ●) are completed, click the blue **Apply** button. The case will move to Resolved status, SLAs will be finalised, and the case will leave the active queue. Click **Cancel** to abort without making changes.

### End-to-End Case Resolution Checklist

✅ Before clicking "Resolved", confirm all of the following:
- Customer's issue has been fully addressed or appropriately escalated
- CRM data was fetched and the order number (if applicable) is noted on the case
- All mandatory fields in the Resolved dialog are filled accurately
- A closing message was sent to the customer (via Canned Response or custom)
- If escalated internally, the relevant team was notified via **@mention** or **Internal Hold** macro
- SLA status shows Response SLA MET where possible

✕

## Microsoft Outlook Folder Setup

### How to set up Outlook Folders

### 01

Click on Home

### 02

Click On Rules

### 03

Click on Manage Rules

![image](/web/image/3342-c5d1f47d/o1.png)

### 04

Click on + Add new rule

![image](/web/image/3341-149f6e93/o2.png)
05
Name your rule
- In the “Name” field at the top, type something descriptive like “Contact Center”.
- This helps you identify the purpose of the rule later (for example, routing all emails to the Contact Center folder).

06
Add a condition
- Conditions define when the rule should trigger e.g., when an email is received from or to someone specific.
- Here, the condition used is “To” meaning this rule will apply to messages sent to specific email addresses.

07
Choose the email addresses
- Enter the relevant addresses, such as CC_Contact Center and Customer Support.
- Outlook will automatically apply this rule whenever a message is sent to those addresses.

08
Add an action
- Actions define what should happen when the condition is met.
- Here, the action is “Move to” meaning the emails that meet the condition will be moved to a specific folder.

09
Choose the destination folder
- Select the folder where those emails should go in this case, the Contact Center folder.
- You can also create a new folder if needed.

10
Configure rule options
- **Stop processing more rules**: tells Outlook to stop checking other rules once this one runs. (Useful to prevent duplicate actions.)
- **Run rule now:** immediately applies the rule to existing emails that meet the condition.

11
Save the rule
- Click **Save**to activate your rule.
- Once saved, Outlook will automatically start routing matching emails according to the setup.

![image](/web/image/3344-6e003d57/o3.png)

### **Result**

From now on, **any email sent to “CC_Contact Center” or “Customer Support”**will automatically move to the “Contact Center” folder, keeping your inbox organized and reducing manual work.

## To check your rules

Go to 1 Mail then 2 Rules

![image](/web/image/3351-729a52f9/o4.png)

### 12

To Add to Favorites:

Right Click on Inbox and choose Add favorite

![image](/web/image/3353-9b943bb2/o5.png)

### 13

The rule labeled “Contact Center” automatically moves or filters emails that meet certain conditions (like being sent to or from “CC_Contact Center” or “Customer Support”) into the Contact Center folder shown on the left sidebar.

![image](/web/image/3352-56ffc9a2/o6.png)

### Microsoft Outlook Rules

What They Are & Why They Matter

What Are Outlook Rules?
Outlook Rules are automated actions that help you organize, sort, and manage your emails without manual effort. They run automatically when messages arrive (or when you send them), saving time, reducing clutter, and ensuring you never miss important messages.

Main Types of Outlook Rules
| **Sent Rules** | Triggered when you send an email. | Move all sent emails with attachments to an “Attachments Sent” folder. |
| --- | --- | --- |

|  |
| --- |

| **Inbox Rules** | Automatically handle incoming messages based on conditions (e.g., sender, subject, keywords). | Move all emails from your manager to a “Priority” folder. |
| --- | --- | --- |

Common Uses for Outlook Rules
**Organize Emails**

- Move messages from specific senders to dedicated folders.
- Example: Move all “noreply@” emails to an “Automated Notifications” folder.

**Highlight Important Messages**

- Mark emails from your manager or certain projects with a color or flag.

**Declutter Automatically**

- Delete or archive newsletters, promotions, or spam messages automatically.

**Stay Notified**

- Set alerts or play sounds for VIP senders (e.g., Leaders, Supervisors, Managers, or Director).

**Manage Sent Items**

- Copy or move specific sent messages (like reports) into project folders.

**Team Collaboration**

- Forward incoming customer requests to a shared mailbox or teammate.

**Reporting & Tracking**

- Automatically categorize or flag emails containing certain keywords (e.g., “urgent,” “invoice,” “training”).

Tips for Using Rules Efficiently
- **Order matters:** Outlook runs rules from top to bottom — arrange them by priority.
- **Avoid conflicts:** Make sure two rules don’t act on the same message in different ways.
- **Limit rule size:** There’s a maximum server storage for Exchange/Outlook Web rules (~256KB).
- **Test your rules:** Run them manually first to confirm they behave as expected.
- **Use conditions wisely:** Combine conditions like “from + subject + has attachments” for precision.

- The status of the ticket, Ex. Assign, Pending, Closed.....

Ticket Id
- The ticket Number.

Note: Using the ticket Id you can search for that specific ticket incase the order number containing the was not available.

Assigned User
- The name of the employee that the ticket is assigned to.

Greeting / Associate identified self and company
+2

#### Measures / What to do

- Send in sequence:
1) شكرا لتواصلك مع بوتيكات...
2) معك ‎{Agent First Name}
3) كيف بإمكاني مساعدتك ؟ (if the customer didn't send their complaint yet)
- If the customer already provided details and the contact became a drop, you may continue without greeting again (same session).

Offered assistance to the customer (Opening protocol)
+1

#### Measures / What to do

- If the agent sent the greeting the same minute as the customer, the score stays.
- Not applicable if the inquiry/request/complaint was sent in the first or multiple messages.

Associate in control of the chat (Proper chat sequence)
+3

#### Measures / What to do

- Opening sequence (no pause required):
1) Greetings (التحية)
2) Inform about survey link (مقدمة)
- Waiting for customer answer:
1) Wait 3 minutes and 3 seconds
2) If no reply, wait +2:03
3) After total 5:06 with no reply, send ending scripts (تقييم / انهاء / سعيد)

Did the associate follow the Hold Protocol (Duration/Usage)
+4

#### Measures / What to do

- Hold protocol:
1) Max 3 holds per chat
2) Each hold ≤ 3 minutes
3) Use agreed English/Arabic scripts (مراجعة / انتظار)
4) Do not change the time in scripts
5) To hold again: send unhold → hold

Customer's name & Proper Titles
+1

#### Measures / What to do

- Use proper titles at least once: Dear customer, Dear [name], عميلنا العزيز, etc.
- Use the name from the interaction (not necessarily the order).

Offer further assistance before closing (service script)
+2

#### Measures / What to do

- Give 1:03 after last answer for customer reply.
- Send service script offering further assistance before closing.

Inform customer about feedback link (opening & ending)
+2

#### Measures / What to do

- Send (مقدمة) at start.
- Send (تقييم) at end.

Inform customer of ending & send wishes (ending + wish scripts)
+1

#### Measures / What to do

- Send (انهاء) at end.
- Send (سعيد) at end.

#### Communication · Total: 25 pts

Respectful, professional, personalized empathy; avoid jargon
+5

#### Measures / What to do

- Use polite professional language.
- Apologize sincerely if it's company fault.
- Thank for patience/cooperation.
- Personalize apology to the issue.
- Avoid repeating same script — explain clearly.

Timely responses & proactivity
+5

#### Measures / What to do

- Respond within 3 minutes with an answer or a follow‑up question.
- If you can’t, use hold script to avoid “dead air.”
- Agents can handle up to 3 chats simultaneously.
- Proactive updates may replace hold (e.g., “I’m still checking for you…”). This resets the 3‑minute timer.

Grammar, spelling, typos & correcting mistakes – 1st time
+2

#### Measures / What to do

- Politely correct spelling/grammar after sending the message.
- Repeat mistakes must still be corrected, but only the first valid correction counts.
- Evaluator highlights mistakes in neutral yellow to confirm validity.
- Multiple mistakes in the same message count as one for scoring.

Grammar, spelling, typos & correcting mistakes – 2nd time
+2

#### Measures / What to do

- Corrections will be monitored; repeated mistakes require correction, but do not count as valid correction again.

Chat as you speak / Avoid robotic tone (Proper chat handling)
+5

#### Measures / What to do

- Use a natural, friendly tone.
- Show active listening and empathy.
- Third time for grammar/typo mistakes (valid corrections will not count).
- Acknowledge the customer's communication & emotions.

Use agreed scripts in correct sequence – 1st time
+3

#### Measures / What to do

- Use system scripts correctly.
- Add helpful details to fit the situation.

Use agreed scripts in correct sequence – 2nd time
+3

#### Measures / What to do

(No measures listed)

#### Problem Solving · Total: 10 pts

Probing / Clear reasoning / Informative & helpful
+5

#### Measures / What to do

- Probe to investigate and find the best solution.
- Explain reasons behind processes when needed.
- Be clear and informative about actions taken (give high‑level details when necessary).
- Summarize next steps and confirm what’s already been done.

Reduce customer effort / Avoid customers repeating themselves
+5

#### Measures / What to do

- Look for opportunities to reduce customer effort (even if extra agent steps).
- Don’t ask for info already in internal systems (CRM, Ameyo), except safety questions.
- If multiple questions in one message, respond to all — not just the first.

#### Update Systems & Ticket Opening · Total: 44 pts

No CRM Call Status
+10

#### Measures / What to do

- For every interaction where an order is mentioned, inquired about, or any action is taken related to it, create a call log with the correct reason and relevant details.
- Each order mentioned in the interaction must have a separate call log.
- Add the call log during the interaction or within 5 minutes after it ends.

Wrong CRM Call Status Reason
+5

#### Measures / What to do

(No measures listed)
Wrong Type CRM Call Status
+3

#### Measures / What to do

(No measures listed)
Wrong/Incomplete Comment CRM Call Status
+3

#### Measures / What to do

- Briefly comment on all key actions taken so any other agent reviewing the case can clearly understand what has been done for the customer.

Ticket Status & Procedures
+15

#### Measures / What to do

- For cases that do not require any further follow‑up, close the Ameyo ticket immediately (max 15 minutes).
- Keep the Ameyo ticket in Follow Up status until the customer’s complaint is fully resolved—regardless of how many agents are involved.

Wrong/Incomplete/Missing Order# / Phone# / SKU#
0

#### Measures / What to do

(No measures listed)
Wrong/Missing Ameyo Contact Reason
+5

#### Measures / What to do

- Select the most relevant reason for the customer’s contact and keep it consistent between CRM and Ameyo when possible.
- For order‑related cases, prioritize complaint reasons over request/inquiry reasons.

Contact Information (Country & Contact Language) + Escalate To
+3

#### Measures / What to do

- Select the country based on the order’s country first; if not available, use the customer’s contact country.
- If the conversation includes both Arabic and English, mark the contact language as Arabic.
- If any internal/external action is taken, update Escalate To with the relevant department.
- If the case is resolved on the floor without escalation, select “Non‑Escalation‑Case.”

#### Assessment of Systematic Procedures

Did the agent follow correct procedures / Using agreed templates (email, ticket)
-15

#### Measures / What to do

(No measures listed)
CCA didn't solve the problem / Ownership / Failure in handling
-15

#### Measures / What to do

(No measures listed)
Abuse – Critical with action
0

#### Measures / What to do

- Customer Abuse Category:
- 1) Force‑closing an active contact without clear visual evidence of a system failure.
- 2) Failing to close a completed contact after conversation ends:
- Calls: open > 4s after last customer response
- Chats: open > 2m after the last message sent by the agent
- 3) Transferring contact to another agent without a valid reason.
- 4) Transferring the interaction ticket to another agent, even if the ticket is empty.
- 5) Merging tickets from different interactions (causes confusion/loss of context).

Wrong / Incomplete / Missing (Process / Policy / SLA / Escalation)
0

#### Measures / What to do

- Avoid unnecessary email traffic — reply within the original department thread.
- Follow‑up every 24h (next working day). Update earlier only if relevant.
- All communications (internal/external) must be professional, clear, to the point.

Further follow‑up on case & further communication with the customer
0

#### Measures / What to do

- Update customer every 24h unless requested otherwise.
- No need to repeat an update already sent by another agent.
- Even with no progress, update to show ownership and SLA commitment.
